clue.text: Flying Wilbur sounds OK

indicators.note: sounds says the word for OK is to be heard rather than written as spelt

parts.note: OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the aviator Wilbur is doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilbur Wright flew the first powered aeroplane with his brother Orville in 1903; 'sounds' tells you the word for OK is heard, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilbur, the pioneer aviator, bore this surname with his brother Orville.

clue.text: Gaiety girl's last fling for equality

indicators.note: a fling throws things about, so the letters of the words before are scattered into a new order
last points to the final letter of the word girl's

explanation.surface: A showgirl from the Gaiety Theatre has one final fling, all in the name of fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes L from 'girl's', and 'fling' scrambles GAIETY with that L. The Gaiety was a famous London musical theatre with chorus girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Egality is an old word for the state of everyone being equal in standing or rights.

clue.text: How the dentist finished off the aching tooth?

definitions.text: How the dentist finished off the aching tooth?

parts.words: How the dentist finished off the aching tooth?
parts.note: a dentist who filled the tooth also brought the pain to an end, so one phrase covers both the filling and the halt

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works two ways: to stop a tooth is to fill its cavity, and 'stopped it' also means put an end to the ache.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist's filling was once called a stopping, so the phrase describes filling the hole and also halting the pain.

clue.text: Awkward age? Try to be revolutionary

indicators.note: awkward suggests something clumsily put together, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone at a gawky stage of life is urged to rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks political, but here it means turning round and round; 'Awkward' is the anagram signal, not a description of the age.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolution is turning in circles, and to spin round a centre is what this verb describes.

clue.text: A toothy insect observed to be airborne

parts.note: observed means saw, past tense of see
to be airborne is to fly

explanation.surface: Someone notices an insect with teeth taking to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The female of this insect has a toothed, saw-like egg-laying tube, which earns 'toothy'.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is named for the serrated ovipositor the female uses to cut into plants.

clue.text: A Rugby man to keep at a distance

explanation.surface: A rugby player is told to stay well back.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the stand-off (fly-half) is the player linking scrum-half and backs. 'To stand off' is to hold oneself away.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the position is the fly-half; as a verb phrase it means to hold back and remain apart.

clue.text: Reputedly witty fellow on a four-wheeled platform, perhaps

parts.note: a wag is a joker, someone known for wit

explanation.surface: A man said to be funny stands on a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart with four wheels for carrying loads is one kind of this vehicle; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: A fall that changes contours, naturally

definitions.text: A fall that changes contours, naturally

parts.words: A fall that changes contours, naturally
parts.note: a slide of earth down a hillside alters the shape of the land, and nature does it, not people

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests a tumble or autumn, but it is a mass of ground slipping down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: When soil and rock slide downhill they reshape the terrain, a natural collapse of ground.

clue.text: Obviously no watcher for the Left!

definitions.text: Obviously no watcher for the Left!

parts.words: Obviously no watcher for the Left!
parts.note: an organ of sight on the opposite side of the face plainly cannot be the left one; read politically it sounds like a person who never looks leftward

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a politics column, someone on the right who ignores the Left; literally it is the eye on the other side of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a person's two eyes, the one on the side opposite the left is plainly not the left one.

clue.text: Pushing forward to the drinks counter, Ginger has no hesitation

parts.note: a bar is the counter where drinks are served

indicators.note: has no says a part is taken out of the word ginger

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone called Ginger shoves straight to the bar without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' looks like a nickname for a redhead pushing to the bar; it is the word to be trimmed, and 'hesitation' is the noise ER, which 'has no' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge is to shove one's way rudely ahead, so this participle means elbowing onward.

clue.text: Some lively footwork when eight pints shortly get to work

parts.note: eight pints make a gallon, shortened to its abbreviation gal
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: After a gallon of beer, someone starts dancing energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' signals the abbreviation GAL for gallon (eight pints); OP is opus, a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A galop is a fast nineteenth-century ballroom dance, so it is quick dancing steps.

clue.text: Quality of the late sardines repacked after initial tampering

indicators.note: after puts the repacked fish behind the initial letter
initial picks the first letter of the word tampering
repacked says the letters of sardines go back in a different order

explanation.surface: A tin of sardines has been tampered with and put back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the late' reads as dead people or a recent tin; here it is people who are late, and the quality is their slowness. 'after' puts the scrambled fish behind the initial T.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness is the state of those who arrive behind time, the quality of being slow.

clue.text: The girl with degree in motoring organisation

indicators.note: in places the degree inside the motoring body's letters

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring club

explanation.surface: A young woman with a qualification works for a car club.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA (Automobile Association) is a British breakdown and motoring organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Head of the French herd curiously tied to post

indicators.note: curiously means oddly arranged, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: tete is the French word for head

explanation.surface: The French leader's cattle are oddly secured to a stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of the' tempts you to take T; instead 'Head of the French' is TETE, French for head. 'curiously' scrambles TETE with HERD.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal fastened by rope to a stake is restrained in this way.

clue.text: A princely-sounding stimulus

indicators.note: sounding says the word is heard, the name rather than its spelling

parts.note: Philip is a prince's name, as with Prince Philip

explanation.surface: Something like a prince gives a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Philip, the late Duke of Edinburgh, supplies the name; said aloud it matches the word for a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is something that gives a lift or encouragement, a spur.

clue.text: Possibly tinier little working model going from place to place

indicators.note: possibly signals that tinier may be rearranged

parts.note: the ant is a small worker held up as a model of industry

explanation.surface: A tiny working scale model travels around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TINIER to ITINER; the ant, Proverbs' example to the sluggard, is the small model of hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant person travels from town to town rather than settling.

clue.text: Assembly makes careful study about Greek points

indicators.note: about says the study word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to con is to study closely, so cons
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A meeting is examining Greek arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: CONS goes 'about' GR plus ES, giving CON-GRES-S. 'Points' are compass points here.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress is a formal gathering of delegates, such as the US legislature.

clue.text: Four yellow-headed leaves may cover the trunk

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: headed means only the head, the first letter, of yellow is used

explanation.surface: Four yellow-topped leaves might grow over a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow-headed' gives Y, the head of 'yellow'. The definition is descriptive: this climber's leaves cover tree trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen climber grows up walls and trees, its foliage smothering the bark.

clue.text: A measure that rates the bullet?

definitions.text: A measure that rates the bullet?

parts.words: A measure that rates the bullet?
parts.note: a bullet is judged by how fast it travels; rate here means speed

explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' looks like grading, but rate is speed: the measure is how fast the bullet goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed in a given direction is how a projectile's flight is measured.

clue.text: What is afoot behind the helmsman?

definitions.text: What is afoot behind the helmsman?

parts.words: What is afoot behind the helmsman?
parts.note: the area towards the stern, at the back of the person steering, is what lies at foot of the ship behind them

explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' suggests something going on; read as 'a foot', it is a position on a ship towards the stern, behind whoever steers.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the stern direction is toward the back, where the steering position faces away from.

clue.text: Make a present of an ode about a beating heart

indicators.note: about means around and astir, so the letters are moved about
heart picks the central letter of the word beating

explanation.surface: Someone gives a poem about a pounding heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes T, the middle letter of 'beating'; 'about' mixes it with AN ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something as a gift, such as money to charity.

clue.text: Sappers turning up to right mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the RE (Royal Engineers) are the army's sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers appear and set a mistake right.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are the Royal Engineers, RE; 'turning up' reverses it in this down entry to ER, then R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go wrong; the verb means slip up.

clue.text: What makes rings to Welsh companion of Johnson

annotationWithheld.why: What makes rings to Welsh companion of Johnson (7): BELL around OS and W needs 'rings' both inside BELL's clue and as OS; no reading found that gives every word one job
annotationWithheld.clue: What makes rings to Welsh companion of Johnson

clue.text: Deviating Croatian worn out, under a cloud

indicators.note: deviating means straying from the usual course, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: A wandering Croatian, exhausted and gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under a cloud' suggests disgrace, but it is literally what this coat is worn under, when it rains.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat is put on in wet weather, beneath grey skies.

clue.text: Teetotaller in a rage to dress

indicators.note: in puts the teetotaller inside the other letters

parts.note: ire is anger
TT is short for teetotal

explanation.surface: A non-drinker in a fury goes to get dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To attire is to clothe someone, as a verb.

clue.text: A householder who doesn't live under his own roof?

definitions.text: A householder who doesn't live under his own roof?

parts.words: A householder who doesn't live under his own roof?
parts.note: a person who occupies a home but rents it, so the roof belongs to a landlord

explanation.walkthrough: 'householder' suggests owner, but the occupier pays rent for a roof that is someone else's.
explanation.definitionFit: A renter occupies property owned by a landlord.

clue.text: Some of the swag in courtyard crowned Henry's victory

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the loot in the yard crowned a king's triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry V's 1415 victory over the French; it is hidden across 'swAG IN COURTyard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V won this famous 1415 battle in France, the triumph that crowned his reign.

clue.text: Troubled reign taking its course in W. Africa

definitions.text: taking its course in W. Africa

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A turbulent reign runs its course in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a river's course: the definition describes the West African river.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of West Africa flows its course through several countries there.

clue.text: Rose family tree creating an ugly squabble for a start

indicators.note: for a start says the squabble comes first, before an

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A family tree causes an unpleasant quarrel from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose family tree' reads like a genealogy of a family named Rose; it is a tree of the botanical rose family.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash belongs to the Rosaceae, the botanical family that includes roses.

clue.text: Where the jockey learns how much he's lost on a race

definitions.text: Where the jockey learns how much he's lost on a race

parts.words: Where the jockey learns how much he's lost on a race
parts.note: a rider is weighed after racing, so 'lost' is lost weight rather than lost money

explanation.walkthrough: 'lost on a race' suggests a lost bet; it is the weight a rider sheds, checked on the scales after the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Jockeys are weighed before and after racing at a set point on the course.

clue.text: Father has an unusual link with an early American statesman

parts.note: FR is short for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A priest has a strange connection with a founding father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns LINK into KLIN. Benjamin Franklin helped draft the US Declaration of Independence and was a diplomat in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin was a founder of the United States.

clue.text: A homeless pet out of one's reckoning

parts.note: a stray is an animal without an owner

explanation.surface: A homeless pet has lost its way.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off course or wide of the mark is to wander off the right path.
